chunks: And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said:

A child is nurtured for seven years, disciplined for seven years, and employed for seven years. The limit of his physical growth is at twenty-three years, and that of his intellect at thirty-five years. Whatever is after that is through experiences.

key_terms.الصَّبِيُّ: the child or young boy in the stage of upbringing
key_terms.مُنْتَهَى طُولِهِ: the utmost extent of physical growth
key_terms.يُؤَدَّبُ: is disciplined and taught proper conduct
key_terms.يُرَبَّى: is nurtured and raised with care
key_terms.يُسْتَخْدَمُ: is given responsibility and put to work or service

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali عليه السلام describe the stages of a child's upbringing and human maturity?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines stages in a child's upbringing: nurture, discipline, and responsibility, each across seven-year periods. It also distinguishes between physical maturation and intellectual completion, emphasizing that later development is shaped by lived experience.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4746 - The Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:

"A child should be nurtured for seven years, disciplined for seven years, and then employed (given responsibility) for seven years. His physical growth reaches its peak at twenty-three years, and his intellect matures at thirty-five years. Whatever comes after that is through experiences."
